description: Hand-curated one-row content mapping for NYSC COURSE-063 Dress Making Without Blocks. The comparison does not establish equivalence to the unverified block-free method.
method: The NYSC column was assessed only from its single governed clothing heading. The approved display correction removes its weekend scheduling clause for display; attendance is not a competency and is not scored. Comparator cells assess garment scope only.

methodology.DOCUMENTED: The cited stored text explicitly names the competency. Coverage is FULL only where every component in category_components is named; otherwise it is PARTIAL.
methodology.FULL: Every listed component of the competency category is explicitly named in the cited evidence.
methodology.PARTIAL: Only part of the category, or a broader/lower-level activity, is explicitly documented.
methodology.NOT_EXPLICIT: The competency is not documented within the available assessed source scope.
methodology.INSUFFICIENT_DATA: Missing or incomplete material prevents reliable assessment.
methodology.caution: This published-text comparison does not prove what is or is not taught.
methodology.areas_rule: Areas to Investigate list NYSC NOT_EXPLICIT competencies documented with FULL coverage by at least two comparator records from at least two countries. PARTIAL evidence does not count.
decisions: The single governed clothing heading is retained as one category; the title’s 'Without Blocks' wording is an unresolved method constraint, not an additional competency row.
The weekend clause is preserved in the cited governed text and removed only by the existing approved display correction; comparator attendance is not scored.
All three sources use patterns, and the Sri Lankan and Philippine sources explicitly use blocks or block patterns; none supports block-free method equivalence.
The TESDA qualification is PARTIAL because its assessed scope establishes women’s casual apparel but not children’s clothing.

evidence.text: Women and children clothing which will be held on weekends.

NYSC-COURSE-063.note: The schedule clause is preserved in governed text and excluded from the displayed competency by an existing approved correction. The block-free method remains unverified.

evidence.text: This unit covers the competencies required to select appropriate needle gauge and required Stitches per inch (SPI), and thread tension to suit the required seams (machines or hand) on fabric & garment, and sew ladies’ basic blouses, skirts and frock using tools , fabric and equipment safely and economically.
Trousers coming under this unit may include Childrens’ trousers; Mens, trousers; Ladies trousers; Slacks/pants

LK-TVEC-NCS-TAILOR-R2-2017.note: Women’s garments and children’s trousers are explicit, but the appended curriculum uses blocks and is not method-equivalent.

evidence.text: Tailor, General: makes ladies and gents' garments and children's clothes by stitching various components together according to pattern, by hand or sewing machine.

IN-DGT-CTS-SEWING-TECHNOLOGY-V2.note: Both clothing components are explicit, but the curriculum uses patterns and is not method-equivalent.

evidence.text: The DRESSMAKING NC II Qualification consists of competencies that a person must achieve to enable him/her to draft and cut pattern; lay-out pattern on the material/fabric, sew material/fabric and apply finishing touches on the ladies casual apparel of the Garment sector.

PH-TESDA-DRESSMAKING-NC2-2005.note: Women’s casual apparel is explicit, children’s clothing is not, and block-pattern use prevents method equivalence.
